item.description: Norwegian guitarist and composer Kim Myhr makes music based on an orchestral exploration of the guitar and has been nominated for both the Nordic Music Prize and the Norwegian Grammys, (Borealis Festival 2024 notes.) In mid-March of 2024, he presents a new work for the opening of the Borealis festival, for no less than fifty 12-string guitars. item.title: How Minneapolis Taught America to Fight Back
item.description: In a Minnesota town outside the Twin Cities, Emily is a nurse who treats many immigrant patients. She can’t locate a patient who just had a test result that shows they might have cancer. item.title: Best Of: Fighting for free press in Russia / ‘Fear and Fury’
item.description: Julia Loktev’s latest documentary, ‘My Undesirable Friends - Part 1: Last Air in Moscow,’ follows independent Russian journalists in the months leading up to, and just after, Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. item.title: Bruce Brubaker Plays Eno and Glass at National Sawdust
item.description: Bruce Brubaker plays Glass and Eno at National SawdustFeb. 12. 7:30PM. $48.67 Pianist Bruce Brubaker wanted to play the music of Brian Eno. But Eno’s ambient music was built around tape loops, electronics, and studio trickery. So Brubaker devised a way to turn the piano into what he refers to as a “supernatural synthesizer,” using electromagnets to bow the strings inside the instrument and using spatialization technology. item.title: OKAN at BAM’s Adam Space
item.description: OKAN at BAM’s Adam SpaceFeb. 12. 7PM. FREE.The Afro-Cuban duo known as OKAN is now based in Canada, and their music combines the traditional chants and rhythms of the Afro-Cuban tradition with the sounds of contemporary pop and jazz. Both musicians, Elizabeth Rodriguez and Magdelys Savigne are classically-trained on violin and percussion, respectively, and are both initiates of the Afro-Cuban religion Santeria.
